what_it_does: The grades a score adds up: P(2)+P(3), planned and committed.
What a sentence-level question sends: sentence (the sentence with its lead-in, section and component) or paragraph (the paragraph too). Changing it re-asks every sentence.
Items a request carries (0 = one a request; $WBG_ASK_BATCH overrides).
Characters a batched request may hold.
Characters one item's request may hold before its questions are split over several.
Starting gate for the asset map until the skip rule fits one: a sentence is asked an asset at this cosine to its phrases or above, or when a word pattern matches.
A sentence has an asset of its own at this posterior or above (read at publish).

A committed, digital sentence whose best first-pass asset is below this (or has none) also gets the chat model's asset opinion (1.01 = every committed, digital sentence). Keep at or above asset.floor. The first pass still wins at asset.floor; the opinion fills only where there is none.
What the asset map's feedback rounds count as a yes (in what is asked).
Paragraph rule: earlier sentences' asset scores summed, each multiplied by this per sentence back; 0 = off.
The decayed sum's own floor (level paragraph).
Every asset at the floor (true) or the best only (false).
Starting gate for a measure until the skip rule fits one.
Also ask a measure's best N sentences by cosine whatever their score; 0 = off.
Share of the graded yes a fitted gate may leave below it.
Graded yes a label needs before its gate is fitted.
Sentences a feedback round asks per label (assets and measures).
A round yielding fewer at the ask floor is the last.
Most feedback rounds for a measure; 0 = off.
Share of the rejected sentences' centroid subtracted from the query (Rocchio).
Most feedback rounds for an asset; 0 = off (the asset map's other round settings are the measures').
Apply the fitted probability layer to the scores (true) or decide on the raw score (false). The evaluation checks the layer out of fold either way.
How sharply similarity counts in the vote of graded sentences.
Also use similarity to the graded yes centroid minus the no centroid.
Fit each decision kind's labels together, one intercept each, shared slopes.
Precision of the normal prior on each standardised slope.
Fewer graded rows than this: no layer.
Fewer graded yes or no than this: no layer for the label.
Leave graded near-copies above this similarity out of the vote; off = only the sentence itself.
Folds (whole projects) for the out-of-fold check.
Fits weight each graded row by its design weight to this power: 0 = every row once; 1 = the reporting weights (which span 2 to 9,000).

The cut the evaluation and a scratch measure's tally read a first-pass score at: a sentence counts as a yes for a measure at this posterior or above. The pipeline's own commitment is the band rule (band.*), which has no per-measure cut.
What a measure's feedback rounds count as a yes when they pick the next sentences to ask (what is asked, not what is decided). Keep at or below band.low.
The evaluation suggests the floor with the most recall at this precision.
A type counts at this P(yes) or above.
Every type at floor.types (true) or the likeliest only.
on: re-propose OTH types from the sentences no approved type reaches; off: keep those already proposed.
Fewest such sentences before OTH types are proposed.
Assets asked of each package: its best this many by cosine.
A package has an asset at this P(yes) or above.
A further floor on the posterior for a sentence to count on the dashboards.
Where a commitment's asset may come from: unit (the sentence, first pass), second_look (the chat model's second look), paragraph, none.
Only Investment Project Financing operations count.
Another project prints a sentence near-identically when its committed sentences hold this share of its word runs.
Words per run when comparing wording (template_share and the dashboards' near-copy test).
The chat model asked for every second look, one item a request, temperature 0. Pinned: another id is another model and re-asks every second look.
Characters of the paragraph a context question sends beside the sentence.

A first-pass score from this up to band.keep is in the band and is committed only when both second looks agree; below it the sentence is not committed. What is asked is band.ask_low to band.ask_high, never narrower than this.
A first-pass score at this or above is committed on its own.
In the band, the decision model asked again with the paragraph beside the sentence must score this or above.
In the band, the chat model's grade (0 to 3) must be this or above, and the context score must also reach band.context. A missing second look is never a yes.

The second look is asked for first-pass scores from here up to band.ask_high (nothing below 0.50 was right in a trial of 40). Keep at or below band.low. Lowering it asks the newly included sentences; raising it asks nothing.

The second look is asked for first-pass scores below this (1.01 = every score from band.ask_low up). Keep at or above band.keep. A look stored above band.keep decides nothing; it is published for reading, and lets band.keep be raised at publish without asking again.
A committed sentence is digital at this P(yes) or above (asked once per sentence, with its paragraph beside it). What decides; what is asked is digital.ask_low.

The measure second looks (the context question and the chat grade) are asked only for sentences whose digital P(yes) is this or above; a sentence with no digital answer yet waits for it. Keep at or below digital.floor (the load fails otherwise). Lowering it asks the sentences it now includes; raising it asks nothing; digital.floor can move anywhere from here up at publish with no further question.

A package-to-asset first-pass P(yes) from here up to link.asset_yes counts when the chat model's second look says yes. What is asked is link.asset_ask_low to link.asset_ask_high, never narrower than this.
The chat model's second look at a package x asset pair is asked for first-pass P(yes) from here up to link.asset_ask_high. Keep at or below link.asset_band_low.
Asked for first-pass P(yes) below this (1.01 = every pair from link.asset_ask_low up). Keep at or above link.asset_yes. Decisions stay link.asset_band_low and link.asset_yes.

A package is strongly linked to a measure at this P(yes) or above, when asked directly about the measure. This is the probability a strong package link shows on the dashboards; a link by shared asset has none.

Measures a package is asked the strong-link question about: its best this many by cosine (its description against the measure's phrases and definition), among the measures its project has a kept sentence for; every pair already answered is kept. Raising it asks the newly included pairs; lowering it asks nothing.
Most sentences of one project x measure group the chat model is shown at once; a larger group is split by document and each part merged separately.
A question the chat model answered unreadably this many times is not asked again and is counted as gave up; it never counts as a yes. Each failed attempt is one row in chat_failures.

Most tokens a chat reply may hold (sent as max_tokens). 1000 is a safety margin: with second.reasoning false a reply is about 10 tokens, but a provider that ignores the switch spends them on hidden reasoning (measured 2026-11-20: at 300, 61 per cent of grade replies were unreadable).

May the chat model reason before it answers the short forms (grade, yes or no, choice, labels, assets)? false: the request carries reasoning enabled false (cheaper, readable replies); true: nothing extra is sent.
Most tokens an activities reply may hold (a longer reply than the other second looks; with reasoning on, 1500 failed for groups of 23 to 39 sentences).

May the chat model reason before it groups sentences into activities? true: nothing extra is sent (measured 2026-11-20: groups better, 4000 tokens needed); false: the request carries reasoning enabled false.
US$ per million prompt tokens, for estimates and for a response that reports no cost.
US$ per million reply tokens, for estimates and for a response that reports no cost.

A procurement plan PDF is read only when at least this share of its table rows carry a borrower reference that is one of the plan's packages (a row whose reference cannot be read counts against it); a plan with scrambled cell text is rejected and keeps the text reading alone.
